title: Adobe just let Claude, ChatGPT & Gemini edit your Photoshop files directly
summary: Adobe updates Photoshop to let external AI agents from Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini edit files directly
detailed: Adobe announced at Adobe MAX 2026 that third-party AI agents like Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini will be authorized to edit native Photoshop, Premiere, and Illustrator files directly.
The upcoming Creative Cloud MCP, heading to private beta in early 2027, allows external agents to modify local files without flattening layers or collapsing sequences.
Adobe introduced the Creative Agent and updated Firefly AI Assistants with planning modes, brand consistency tools, and automated batch editing capabilities.
Adobe expanded enterprise partnerships by bringing Acrobat to Gmail and Google Drive and extending its footprint across Microsoft Windows-based workflows.
sentences: The reveal came on the final day of Adobe MAX 2026, held November 10–12 at the Miami Beach Convention Center, and served as the capstone to a conference that had spent three days making a single sustained argument: agentic AI has moved from the margins of professional creative work into its center.
Adobe MAX 2026 drew creative professionals, enterprise marketers, and social content creators to Miami Beach, with virtual audiences streaming keynotes at max.adobe.com.

The centerpiece product announcement covers the Creative Agent, Adobe's proprietary AI engine, now powering expanded AI Assistants across After Effects, Premiere, Illustrator, InDesign, Frame.io, and Photoshop.

Inside Premiere specifically, the assistant can now apply effects across every clip in a sequence, track masked subjects frame by frame, and correct color and exposure for an entire project in a single operation — tasks that previously consumed hours of manual editing time.
The updated Firefly AI Assistant introduces a trust-centered addition: a planning mode that surfaces the agent's full proposed workflow for user review and editing before any execution begins.
Users can also specify a preferred AI model to orchestrate tasks, or leave that decision to Adobe's software.
A dedicated brand consistency tool rounds out the update — users can now define color palettes and guidelines that persist across every project the assistant handles.
The boldest move of the conference may be the Creative Cloud MCP, previewed at MAX and headed for private beta in early 2027.

The protocol enables outside AI agents — Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini among them — to work directly on native Photoshop, After Effects, Illustrator, and Premiere files stored on a user's local machine, without collapsing layers or flattening sequences into a single image or clip.
The practical implications for professional workflows are significant.

A video editor could, in theory, brief a third-party AI assistant in a chat interface and have it execute targeted changes inside a live After Effects project, with every individual layer remaining available for further human refinement afterward.
Day 2 delivered the conference's most forward-looking session.
Adobe's MAX Sneaks unveiled 10 research projects spanning video, audio, imaging, and design.
The unifying argument was blunt: "Chat is insufficient for precise visual work," Adobe's researchers said.

The majority of the projects on display replace typed prompts with brushes, drags, and physical gestures — a direct acknowledgment that language models alone cannot provide the level of control professional creatives require for exacting visual tasks.
Two of the 10 projects are already accessible in a new Adobe Labs Playground for early testing.
Adobe has not committed to commercial shipping timelines for any of them.
Beyond its own tools, Adobe used MAX to deepen existing enterprise alliances.
Acrobat is coming to Gmail and Google Drive under an expanded Google partnership, while a broader Microsoft deal extends Adobe's footprint across Windows-based workflows.
Both announcements position Adobe less as a standalone software vendor and more as the connective layer of a wider AI creative ecosystem.

Adobe had already confirmed the week before MAX that its CX Enterprise Coworker agent is now available inside ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini for business, Databricks Genie, and Microsoft Copilot, adding a layer of third-party reach to the Creative Cloud announcements made in Miami Beach.
The final day of MAX wrapped sessions and Creative Park activities at 3 p.m.
ET on Thursday, with all keynotes and Sneaks available on demand at max.adobe.com.
